description: The Global Surface Water dataset maps where and when surface water occurred worldwide from 1984 to 2021 and gives statistics on the extent and change of water surfaces. It was produced by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) with Google from 4,716,475 Landsat 5, 7 and 8 scenes acquired between 16 March 1984 and 31 December 2021, each 30 m pixel classified individually as open water or not; layers include water occurrence, occurrence change intensity, seasonality, recurrence, transitions between classes and maximum water extent, plus yearly and monthly water histories. The method is described in the Nature (2016) paper "High-resolution mapping of global surface water and its long-term changes" and a Data Users Guide. Layers are explored in the Global Surface Water Explorer and served in Google Earth Engine (JRC/GSW1_4) and as downloads, free of charge and without restriction of use under the Copernicus Programme, with citation required. Caveats: cloud and terrain shadows cause gaps, water under vegetation or narrower than about 30 m is missed, and early years have fewer observations. It supports mapping of blue infrastructure, wetlands and reservoirs, permanent water masks for flood hazard models, historical flood and drought exposure and climate adaptation studies, and is used as the permanent water mask in the Global Flood Database catalogued here.
